newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Sierra Leone talks seen as unlikely to end crisis.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone talks seen as unlikely to end crisis.

text.p: Delegates from Sierra Leone's military junta held out little hope of resolving the violence in their country as they prepared on Thursday for talks with West African foreign ministers in Ivory Coast.
"We are not going to get a solution today, but let the world start hearing the full story," junta spokesman Allieu Kamara told reporters.

Corporal Tamba Gborie, who led the coup and installed Major Johnny Paul Koroma as military leader, said it would be impossible to strike a deal without rebel leader Foday Sankoh, who remains under effective house arrest in Nigeria.
Koroma has named Sankoh, who was listed on the Freetown delegation, as his number two. "You can't make any peace in Sierra Leone without Foday Sankoh," Gborie said.

Leaders of the May 25 Freetown coup and their allies were in Abidjan to meet ministers from regional power broker Nigeria, Ivory Coast, Ghana and Guinea, who were representing the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS).
Kamara said the junta wanted to publicise what he called the corruption of ousted civilian president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah and fraud that helped him win the 1996 election.
The late-arrival of Nigerian Foreign Minister Tom Ikimi and Ghana's deputy foreign minister, Victor Gbeho, delayed the start of talks. The two were held up in neighbouring Liberia.
Kamara said the ministers would not be staying long enough to reach a deal on Sierra Leone, and were more concerned with Saturday's national elections in Liberia.
"They are returning to Liberia on Saturday," he said.

Other members of the Sierra Leone delegation displayed bitterness towards Nigeria, which commands ECOMOG, an ECOWAS military force in both Liberia and Sierra Leone. They denounced Nigerian belligerence and praised Ghanaian diplomacy.
"We are ready to disarm, but we can't with the Nigerians bombing our country," coup leader Gborie said.
Sierra Leone's neighbours opted in Guinea on June 26 for dialogue and economic sanctions to persuade the junta to reinstate Kabbah. They retained the military option.
Nigerian soldiers have clashed with Sierra Leone troops and their rebel allies on several occasions after Nigerian gunboats bombarded the capital in a June 2 show of force.
The junta's foreign minister, Paolo Bangura, is leading the Freetown delegation.
